Two segments are congruent when their lengths are equal.
\(l(DE) = 9 - (-7) = 16\) and \(l(AB) = 5 - (-3) = 8\).
Since \(16 \ne 8\), seg DE and seg AB are not congruent.

Two segments are congruent when their lengths are equal.
\(l(BC) = 5 - 2 = 3\) and \(l(AD) = -3 - (-7) = 4\).
Since \(3 \ne 4\), seg BC and seg AD are not congruent.

Two segments are congruent when their lengths are equal.
\(l(BE) = 9 - 5 = 4\) and \(l(AD) = -3 - (-7) = 4\).
Since the lengths are equal, seg BE \(\cong\) seg AD, so the segments are congruent.

The midpoint of a segment divides it into two congruent halves, so \(AM = \frac{1}{2} AB\).
\(AM = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 = 4\)

P is the midpoint of seg CD, so \(CP = PD\) and \(l(CD) = 2 \times CP\).
\(l(CD) = 2 \times 2.5 = 5\)

Compare the three lengths: \(2 < 3.4 < 5\).
So \(BP < AP < AB\), that is seg BP \(<\) seg AP \(<\) seg AB.

Ray RP starts at R and goes to the right, through P and Q. Its opposite ray starts at the same point R and goes to the left, through S and T.
The opposite ray of ray RP is ray RS (or ray RT).

Ray PQ starts at P and goes right, so it is the part of the line from P onward through Q. Ray RP starts at R and goes right, so it contains R, P, Q and everything beyond.
The common part of the two rays is the portion from P rightward.
Ray PQ \(\cap\) ray RP \(=\) ray PQ

Seg QR runs from R to Q and so contains the point P, that is seg PQ is a part of seg QR.
Taking the union therefore adds nothing new.
Seg PQ \(\cup\) seg QR \(=\) seg QR

Seg QR is the part of the line between R and Q. Any ray that contains both R and Q contains this whole segment.
Ray QR (starting at Q, going left) and ray RQ (starting at R, going right) both contain seg QR.
Seg QR is a subset of ray QR and of ray RQ, and also of rays such as ray SQ and ray TQ.

Opposite rays have the same end point and go in opposite directions along the line. From R, one ray goes right through P and Q, the other goes left through S and T.
Ray RQ and ray RT are a pair of opposite rays with common end point R (ray RP and ray RS is the same pair).

A ray with end point S is named by S together with any other point of the line on the chosen side of S. To the right of S lie R, P, Q and to the left lies T.
Ray SR and ray ST are two such rays (ray SP and ray SQ also have end point S).

Ray SP starts at S and goes right, through R, P and Q. Ray ST starts at S and goes left, through T. They are opposite rays, so the only point common to both is their common end point.
Ray SP \(\cap\) ray ST \(=\) Point S

The co-ordinate of B is 2, so find the distance of each point from 2.
\(d(A, B) = 2\), \(d(B, C) = 2\); \(d(P, B) = 4\), \(d(B, D) = 4\).
Point A and point C are equidistant from B, and point P and point D are equidistant from B.

The co-ordinate of Q is \(-4\), so find the distance of each point from \(-4\).
\(d(U, Q) = -4 - (-5) = 1\) and \(d(Q, L) = -3 - (-4) = 1\).
Point L and point U are equidistant from Q (point P and point R are another such pair, each at distance 2).

Each distance is the positive difference of the two co-ordinates.
\(d(U, V) = 5 - (-5) = 10\)
\(d(P, C) = 4 - (-2) = 6\)
\(d(V, B) = 5 - 2 = 3\)
\(d(U, L) = -3 - (-5) = 2\)
